questions.text: What does completing this course provide?

options.text: Study of the material without automatic award of a vocational grade
Automatic authorisation for all welded structures
Authority to sign any inspection report
Automatic appointment as the person responsible for lifting equipment

questions.explanation: Fundamentals of welding processes and safe workplace organisation. Joint preparation, equipment, protection and inspection. A training programme for work in the Republic of Kazakhstan.

questions.text: What should be done if a welded-joint requirement is unclear?

options.text: Start and clarify after acceptance
Clarify the requirement before welding
Choose parameters at random
Repeat any previous weld

questions.explanation: Read the drawing and joint requirements before work. Establish the material, edge preparation and welding position. Check the procedure, parameters and inspection requirements. Clarify unclear requirements before welding starts.

questions.text: Why should an unknown coating be assessed before heating?

options.text: To dispense with ventilation
Because every coating protects against fumes
It may produce harmful emissions and affect quality
Only to choose the method of later painting

questions.explanation: Clean surfaces as required by the procedure. Remove contamination that could impair quality or produce harmful emissions. Check edge shape and joint gap. Secure components for stable positioning and safe access.

questions.text: How are the welding machine's power supply and permitted load selected?

options.text: By resemblance to a previously used machine
From the power rating of a different machine on the site
From cable length alone
From the machine passport and instructions

questions.explanation: Transformers, rectifiers and inverters have different characteristics. Verify power supply and permitted load against the equipment passport. Follow the cooling and duty-cycle instructions. Stop in the event of overheating or a fault.

questions.text: What protects the eyes during welding?

options.text: A suitable welding shield or helmet with a filter
Ordinary clear glasses instead of a helmet
Sunglasses without assessment
Limiting the time spent looking at the arc

questions.explanation: Select a welding helmet or shield for the process and parameters. The filter must provide the required protection. Check integrity, attachments and function. Use protection against flying particles during grinding and cleaning.

questions.text: How should welding fumes be removed?

options.text: By smell, switching ventilation on only when the smell is strong
By the specified ventilation with extraction at the source
Only with an open door under all conditions
Only through general air exchange without assessing local extraction

questions.explanation: Remove contaminants as close to their source as possible. General ventilation supplements local extraction. Emissions depend on the metal, coatings and consumables. Select respiratory protection from a risk assessment; it does not replace required ventilation.

questions.text: How should the gas in a cylinder be identified before connection?

options.text: By estimating cylinder weight visually
By matching the thread without checking
From markings and documentation
Only by the cylinder colour

questions.explanation: Identify the gas from markings and documentation. Check the shell, valve and required examination information. Do not use a defective or uncertainly identified cylinder. Colour alone is not sufficient for connection.

questions.text: Where should pressure settings for a torch or cutting torch come from?

options.text: An arbitrary training example
The settings of a different torch
The maximum gauge reading
The instructions for the actual equipment and procedure

questions.explanation: Select a regulator for the gas and pressure range. Use compatible connections without improvised adapters. Check gauge condition and absence of damage. Set operating pressure according to the torch instructions.

questions.text: Can a used container with unknown contents be welded?

options.text: No; identification, preparation and authorisation are required first
Yes, if it looks empty
Yes, if the weld is short
Yes, after wiping the exterior

questions.explanation: Before heating, establish what the container previously held. Remove residues and isolate connected services under the procedure. Test the atmosphere and complete the required authorisation measures. Do not independently weld a closed or unidentified container.

questions.text: What forms part of safe completion of welding?

options.text: Leaving immediately without inspection
Shutdown as instructed, area inspection and the required fire monitoring
Only switching off the power source without inspecting the area
Only closing the gas supply without checking the workplace

questions.explanation: Shut down equipment and the gas system as instructed. Prevent unintended starting and leaks. Inspect the work area and adjacent spaces for smouldering. Record completion and maintain the required fire monitoring.

questions.text: Is an externally even weld sufficient to verify all its properties?

options.text: Yes, if the welder is experienced
Yes, if the metal is still hot
No; acceptance requires the specified inspection
Yes; an even weld is always acceptable

questions.explanation: Welding creates a permanent joint between materials. Required properties depend on the material, structure and operating conditions. Weld appearance does not verify all internal properties. Acceptance follows the requirements for the specific product.

questions.text: How are electrode classification and diameter selected?

options.text: By availability without checking material compatibility
By electrode diameter without checking classification
Always the same for every metal
According to the material and welding procedure

questions.explanation: The consumable electrode contributes to the weld metal. Its coating provides the intended process protection. Select the electrode classification, diameter and parameters using the welding procedure. Electrode condition affects joint quality.

questions.text: How is an unacceptable tack-weld defect handled?

options.text: Remove it by the established method before continuing
Always cover it with the next layer without assessment
Ignore it because it is not a weld
Paint over it before continuing

questions.explanation: Verify component alignment against the drawing. Make tack welds according to material and procedure requirements. Fixtures must hold components without dangerous movement. Remove unacceptable tack-weld defects using the established method.

questions.text: What should be done with damaged welding-cable insulation?

options.text: Increase current to check the contact
Remove the defective part from use until corrected
Continue in gloves without checking
Cover the damage with a wet cloth

questions.explanation: Check insulation, connections and electrode clamping. Protect cables from heat, cuts and moving vehicles. Place the holder to prevent accidental short circuits. Remove defective components from use.

questions.text: Which clothing condition is unsuitable for welding?

options.text: No exposed areas of skin
Specified protection of footwear against particles
Contamination with combustible substances
Protection against sparks and hot particles

questions.explanation: Clothing must protect against sparks and hot particles. Use welding gloves and keep them dry. Prevent exposed skin and pockets that collect sparks. Footwear and clothing arrangement must keep hot metal out.

questions.text: Who connects and repairs the machine?

options.text: Any learner after viewing the presentation
Any colleague without checking authority
Only whoever first notices the fault
Authorised personnel within their authorisation

questions.explanation: Authorised personnel connect the machine using the established method. Check protective connections and cables before work. Do not work with damaged equipment or unsafe moisture conditions. Repairs and switching require the relevant separate authorisation.

questions.text: Why must oxygen fittings be kept free from oil and grease?

options.text: Oxygen increases fire hazards
Because removing oil replaces a leak-tightness check
Only to improve gauge accuracy
Only to prevent mechanical wear of threads

questions.explanation: Oxygen supports combustion and increases fire hazards. Fuel gas can form a dangerous mixture with air. Keep oxygen fittings free from oil and grease. Never use oxygen to blow off clothing or ventilate a space.

questions.text: How should a leak at a gas connection be located?

options.text: By heating the connection until a smell appears
By an approved method without an open flame
With a lighter
With the welding arc

questions.explanation: Use hoses suitable for the gas and working conditions. Protect them from kinks, sparks and mechanical damage. Use the specified fasteners for connections. Check leaks by an approved method without an open flame.

questions.text: How is a fall-protection attachment point selected?

options.text: Use the first available pipeline
Use the welding cable
Follow the established system and verified anchorage points
Use any scaffold component based on appearance

questions.explanation: Use a safe platform and the specified fall protection. Select attachment points under the established system, not arbitrarily. Protect fall-protection components from sparks and hot metal. Barrier off the lower area against falling objects and particles.

questions.text: After a pop, the torch operates unstably. What should be done?

options.text: Continue until complete failure
Remove the protective valve
Independently increase pressure without checking
Stop as instructed and correct the cause before restarting

questions.explanation: Flashback carries the flame back towards the gas system. Specified valves and flashback arrestors reduce the risk. Stop according to the instructions after a pop, overheating or unstable operation. Restart only after establishing and correcting the cause.

questions.text: What determines the choice of welding process?

options.text: Material, thickness and the welding procedure
Only the operator's preference
Only the required working speed
Only the available machine, regardless of material

questions.explanation: An electric arc provides heat in arc welding. Gas welding uses the flame of fuel gas and oxygen. Weld-pool protection depends on the selected process. Select the process according to material, thickness and procedure.

questions.text: What additional hazard does shielding gas create?

options.text: It eliminates all electrical hazards
It can displace oxygen from the work area
It always makes the atmosphere safe to breathe
It completely removes the need for ventilation

questions.explanation: The process uses wire or a non-consumable electrode, depending on its type. Gas shields the weld pool from the surrounding atmosphere. Interrupted gas supply can impair quality. Select the gas and flow rate according to the procedure and equipment. Shielding gas can displace oxygen from the work area.

questions.text: How should a change in welding parameters be handled?

options.text: Always set maximum current
Copy parameters from any neighbouring station
Justify it against procedure requirements
Change randomly until the appearance is attractive

questions.explanation: Select current, voltage and travel speed using the procedure. Account for welding position, thickness and the component's thermal condition. Any parameter change must be justified. Pass sequence helps control shape and distortion.

questions.text: Can a random pipeline replace the work return conductor?

options.text: Yes, if the pipeline is metal
Yes, for a short weld
Yes, if it runs closer to the machine
No; the intended welding circuit is required

questions.explanation: Current must return through the intended welding circuit. Provide a reliable connection to the workpiece. Do not substitute random pipes or structures for the return conductor. Apply the special insulation requirements in fire or explosion hazardous conditions.

questions.text: Why are screens used around the welding area?

options.text: To protect others from the arc and particles
To replace the welder's helmet
To dispense with ventilation
Only to conceal the work being performed

questions.explanation: Separate the welding area with the specified screens. Prevent unprotected people from looking directly at the arc. Check where sparks and particles travel. Keep access routes clear and easy to identify.

questions.text: Why are openings and concealed spaces checked during hot work?

options.text: To end monitoring as soon as the machine is switched off
Sparks can cause smouldering outside the visible area
So checking adjacent spaces can replace removal of combustible materials
Only to check whether workers can pass through

questions.explanation: Obtain the prescribed authorisation for temporary hot work. Remove or protect combustible materials. Check openings and adjoining spaces. Provide firefighting equipment and the required monitoring.

questions.text: How should a gas cylinder be moved?

options.text: By striking its body
By freely rolling it down stairs
With equipment intended for the purpose, protected against falling and damage
By the valve

questions.explanation: Secure cylinders against falling and protect them from heat. Use equipment intended for cylinder handling. Do not lift by the valve or expose cylinders to impacts. Determine separation distances and co-location from current requirements.

questions.text: Can work continue after flashback without a check?

options.text: Yes, if the flame has recovered
Yes, after removing the flashback arrestor
Yes, if an extinguisher is nearby
No; stop and correct the cause

questions.explanation: Flashback carries the flame back towards the gas system. Specified valves and flashback arrestors reduce the risk. Stop according to the instructions after a pop, overheating or unstable operation. Restart only after establishing and correcting the cause.

questions.text: What is required for welding in a confined space?

options.text: Special preparation, authorisation, atmosphere testing and rescue measures
Only moving the machine inside
Only an open hatch without assessment
Only a colleague's presence without communication

questions.explanation: Entry requires special preparation and established authorisation. Arrange atmosphere testing, ventilation, communication and an attendant. Plan rescue without improvisation. Stop and leave if conditions change.

questions.text: What confirms the outcome of a weld-defect repair?

options.text: Only rewelding without checking the result
The required repeat inspection
Only a visual examination instead of the prescribed inspection scope
Only grinding away visible traces

questions.explanation: Supplement visual inspection with the required methods. Record results against the specific joint. Use an agreed procedure for repair. Repeat inspection to confirm the repair result.
